subject: Geography
central_question: How can world climates be classified from temperature and precipitation, and what evidence and processes explain climate change?
in_scope_units: Empirical, genetic and applied climate classification
Koeppen climate-classification scheme and letter codes
Global warming, greenhouse gases, ozone depletion and international response
banned_topics: Detailed daily weather-system mechanics from Chapter 9
Detailed cloud and precipitation processes from Chapter 10
A modern classification replacing the supplied Koeppen scheme

known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter calls it empirical because it is based on observed temperature and precipitation related to vegetation.

known_pitfalls.claim: All five major groups are based only on temperature.
known_pitfalls.correction: Four are temperature-based, while B-Dry is distinguished by precipitation relative to potential evaporation.

known_pitfalls.claim: Climate change is presented only as modern human-caused warming.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter presents long natural variability as well as anthropogenic greenhouse-gas forcing.
Their effectiveness depends on concentration change, atmospheric lifetime and wavelengths absorbed.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 1(ii): identify Koeppen as empirical
NCERT Exercise 2(i): name the two climatic variables used by Koeppen
NCERT Exercise 3(i): compare A and B climates
NCERT Exercise 2(iv): interpret the chapter’s sunspot discussion
NCERT Exercise 3(iii): define and list greenhouse gases
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1, 2 and 3 and Project Work on the Kyoto declaration related to global climate changes.
